text:
jess: quick heads-up — onboarding Tilde's customer finetune (LoRA merge + quant) and seeing weird embedding stability after the merge. putting together a quickpack for triage.

han: ok; can you paste a couple failing examples so we know what "weird" looks like?

jess: sure — small before/after embed snippet (trimmed):
```
input: "Invoice total: $1,250.00"
baseline embed: [0.12, -0.03, 0.07, ...]
post-merge embed: [0.07, -0.10, 0.02, ...]
cos_sim: 0.68 -> 0.51
```

oleg: that's a notable cosine drop. did you run a tokenizer remap or change the embedding head during the LoRA merge?

jess: no explicit tokenizer remap. flow was: merge LoRA -> HF convert -> quantize (AWQ int4). FP16 merged weights tested later — FP16 looks fine.

han: so regression appears only when quantized. can you repro with FP16 merged (no quant) to isolate quant step?

jess: FP16 cos_sim ~0.69, so the big delta shows up after int4. also seeing token-stability glitches on numeric tokens (e.g., "1,250.00" -> tokenized different length post-quant).

oleg: interesting. quantization can amplify small head shifts. try a run with per-channel symmetric vs asymmetric, and toggle per-layer folding. AWQ vs GPTQ might behave differently.

qa-bot: quick-eval summary uploaded:
- dataset: 100 customer prompts (mix invoices, addresses, short dialogs)
- metrics: avg cos_sim pre->post: FP16 delta 0.02, INT4 delta 0.17
- token-stability failures: 12/100 (mostly numeric/amount tokens)
- top failing inputs saved to failing_examples.txt

jess: adding test matrix to quickpack: FP16, INT8, INT4-AWQ(symmetric), INT4-GPTQ, plus tokenizer-diff and no-prefix-cache runs.

han: add a run with prefix cache disabled (to rule out stale KV collisions during our batched smoke tests). also include model logits diff for the failed items.

jess: on it. pushing artifacts to s3: s3://redwood-onboard/tilde/quickpack/1735554321/ (quickpack.tar.gz, eval_summary.csv, failing_examples.txt, quant_config.yaml)

deploy-bot: upload complete — 4 files recorded to s3://redwood-onboard/tilde/quickpack/1735554321/ (uploader: jess)

oleg: I'll spin AWQ config A (symmetric per-channel, no fold) and run a 500-sample mini-batch. will report cos_sim distribution.

han: good. also capture latency and memory numbers — customer cares about cost delta if we recommend FP16 rollback.

jess: plan for triage: 1) repro with AWQ/GPTQ variants 2) try turning off folding in quantizer 3) if still broken, prepare FP16 rollback for initial rollout and notify customer with tradeoffs.

oleg: +1 on rollback as a safe initial posture. also add an eval that shows end-to-end UI rendering for numeric tokens so PMs can see user-facing impact.

han: I'll draft the customer-facing note once we have repro logs — short and prescriptive: what happened, workaround (FP16), ETA for fix.

jess: ETA for first repro attempt ~2h. will update thread with results and attach the quant runs.

han: ping me when results are up and I'll tidy the note.

jess: thanks all — updating now :thumbsup:
